title: Louis Armstrong telling a story with one note
summary: Everybody was listening to Louis, who could swing people with a single note; Dickenson remembers his solo behind a blues singer on record.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Cause you know -- he always -- he usually says he wasn't really listening to Louis then yet. It wasn't until a little after that that he come along with Louis and got a -- sort of got a story as well as his speed.
Yeah. Cause Louis could tell a story with one note. He didn't have to have a whole lot of
notes or nothing -- just that one note would swing people. You know --
Yeah. I guess everybody was listening to Louis then.
You know you told me you heard him pretty early like on records with blues singers and stuff.
Yeah, there was one piece that has lately been revised. I don't know who's the guy that sings it. I can't think of who it was. 'Of All the Wrongs You Done To Me.'
And I heard Louis play that years ago. He played a beautiful solo on it -- you know how the singer stops and lets the guy play a little bit.
I think Beth Shay (PHONETIC) was in that too. (Inaudible).
Was he? I don't know who was on that particular record. I know Louis played it -- a beautiful solo on it.
Yeah. That was before you -- when did you see him live the first time?
Gee, I don't know. I don't know. I have no idea.
